newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Pro-China bankers head HK club to celebrate handover.
newsitem.headline: Pro-China bankers head HK club to celebrate handover.

text.p: Pro-China financiers are heading a new Hong Kong club formed to celebrate the territory's return to Beijing, a line-up analysts said could signal the future hierarchy in the banking and finance industry. The club, the Hong Kong Financial Community Committee for the Celebration of Reunification of Hong Kong with China, was formed this week and is led by six ethnic Chinese financiers who are among the club's 30 or so initiators, a spokesman said.
The club is scheduled to be official inaugurated on Thursday.
Banking analysts said the club committee's structure may help reveal the pecking order among the respective banks in the industry after Britain hands Hong Kong back to China on July 1.
"The Bank of China or China-funded banks will definitely have bigger influence after 1997," said one analyst.
The territory's largest bank, Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd (Hongkong Bank), a unit of London-based HSBC Holdings Plc, is not represented in the decision-making tier of the club.

The bank, founded in 1865, was once a bastion of the colonial order. The committee's six chairmen include executives of two China-funded banks: Yang Zilin, chief executive at the Hong Kong-Macau regional office of the Bank of China, and Chuang Shih-ping, honorary chairman of Nanyang Commercial Bank Ltd.
Robin Chan, a Hong Kong delegate to China's parliament and chairman of Asia Financial Holdings Ltd, is also a chairman of the handover celebration club.
The other three chairmen are Hang Seng Bank Ltd chairman Sir Quo-wei Lee, Bank of East Asia Ltd chairman David Li, and Edgar Cheng, chairman of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Hongkong bank executive director Vincent Cheng, the highest ranking ethnic Chinese at the bank, is a vice-chairman of the club -- one of many in that position -- and not in the ruling council.

The committee's spokesman brushed aside the notion that the club's structure could signal the future standing of Hong Kong banks, saying: "All of them (join) in their personal capacity and do not represent any organisation."
Hongkong Bank's Cheng said Sir Quo-wei, who is also an adviser to the board of HSBC Holdings Plc, could represent Hongkong Bank, the parent of Hang Seng Bank.
"Sir Quo-wei is already a chairman (of the committee)," he said. "We think Mr Lee can represent Hongkong Bank as well, as he represents the entire HSBC group."
"Since the group is already represented at the chairman level, if I became a chairman it would be over-representation," he said. "And it was a personal invitation."
The club's spokesman said members included foreign financiers in the local financial industry, but did not give further details.
